newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM says future profit depends on cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM says future profit depends on cuts.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Friday that future profitability for the mining group would depend on lowering production costs.
"Sustained profitability can be achieved through efforts to continue to pursue our objective of lower costs of production," MIM said in a statement accompanying its half year results.
Earlier MIM announced a half year net loss of A$12 million, down from a A$58.9 million profit a year earlier.

MIM's half year net loss before abnormals and exchange losses was A$8.8 million, down from last year's profit of A$23.6 million, but better than market expectations of a A$10 million to A$20 million loss.

There was an abnormal net loss after tax of A$2.2 million, versus a A$38.9 million profit the previous corresponding year. MIM's Mt Isa operations made a net loss of A$2.5 million, including a A$27.7 million loss from its lead-zinc operations and a A$26.0 million profit from its copper operations.
The copper profit compared with a A$123.2 million profit from copper operations in the same period a year earlier.
Analysts had forecast a A$50 million to A$100 million fall in profits from copper operations.

MIM said the future of the company depended on lowering costs and restoring production levels in the established operations, increasing production at new projects and developing new low cost copper and copper/gold projects.
MIM said the losses were due to lower metal prices, primarily for copper and zinc, and the stronger Australian dollar.

"However, these uncontrollable revenue influences were significantly, but not completely offset by higher sales volumes sourced from all of the mining operations, and lower costs resulting from commendable progress with workplace reform, better integration of mining and improved systems," MIM said.

MIM also cut its dividend to 1.25 cents per share from 2.5 cents. MIM said higher output and lower costs improved Mt Isa's profit by A$50 million, which helped cushion the combined price and exchange rate impact of A$166 million, of which A$149 million was due to copper.
